scope: REINTERPRETATION: the loading object is destroyed on UNLOAD/shutdown, not when loading completes - so its being non-null may be normal and ui_state 5 may not mean 'still loading'

the_teardown_at_0x77d043.0x77D043: cmp [0x8269774], ebx ; je 0x77D092   - if already null, skip
the_teardown_at_0x77d043.0x77D06A: call 0xB82100                         - a method on the object
the_teardown_at_0x77d043.0x77D079: edx = [ecx] ; eax = [edx] ; push 1 ; call eax   - the DELETING destructor (vtable slot 0)

what_this_changes: I had been treating 'the object is non-null' as 'the frontend is still loading'
but the only code that clears it is a teardown path (destructor, guard acquire/release, followed by more shutdown calls)
so while a map is active the object is EXPECTED to be non-null, and its presence is not evidence of loading
which means ui_state = 5 is also not proven to mean 'still loading' - it may simply be the UI state used for both the loading screen and an in-game frame that has nothing to draw
what_that_reopens: the 'world not drawn' hypothesis returns: the client may be in the map with a valid UI state, and the black frame with a spinner may be the absence of scene content rather than an unfinished load
and the spinner could be a UI element that is drawn whenever the renderer has no valid view, rather than a load indicator
how_to_distinguish_the_two: if the client is in the map, then a screenshot after a delay large enough for the frontend to settle should not change, and forcing a screen resize or a dvar change should redraw the same black frame
conversely if it is still loading, the spinner should animate - and capturing two screenshots a second apart and comparing them will show whether the spinner moved
that is a cheap and decisive test: two captures, one second apart, compared pixel-wise
